title: High protein chocolate mousse
summary: Paneer blended with melted dark chocolate until there is no trace of the paneer left, then set in the fridge. About 26 g of protein a serving, and it pipes well enough to top a cake.

time.note: Plus at least 2 hours setting in the fridge. The video waited three.

nutrition_per_serving.note: Made with full-fat paneer. Firm tofu instead brings this to roughly 390 calories and 22 g protein.

ingredients.note: The body of the mousse. It has to blend to a completely smooth cream - anything that stays grainy stays grainy in the finished dish.
This is what sets the mousse firm in the fridge, not the paneer. Leave it out and you get chocolate paneer paste that never firms up.
Without this the blender will not move the paste at all.
Not optional. Unsalted chocolate tastes flat and slightly chalky.

steps: Melt the dark chocolate - 30 seconds in the microwave, stir, then 15 seconds at a time until it just goes liquid. Overheated chocolate seizes into a grainy lump and will not come back.
Put the paneer, cocoa, honey, salt and vanilla into a blender jar.
Pour in the melted chocolate and the milk. Add the liquid before you blend, not after - a dry paneer-and-cocoa paste will jam a blender and climb the sides instead of turning over.
Blend until completely smooth, stopping to scrape the sides down. Give it longer than feels necessary; any grain left now is grain in the set mousse.
Pour into a bowl or two glasses, cover with cling film pressed onto the surface so it does not form a skin, and refrigerate at least 2 hours until set.
tips: A small bullet blender will struggle with this and stall - the paste is stiff before the milk goes in. A full jar mixer grinder handles it comfortably. If a bullet jar is all you have, blend the paneer with the milk alone first, then add everything else.
Set firm, it holds a piped rosette, so it works as a cake or cupcake topping and as a thick spread.
No microwave: melt the chocolate in a bowl set over a pan of just-simmering water, and keep water out of the bowl.
Firm tofu works in place of paneer and takes it down to roughly 390 calories a serving, but it is blander - taste it before it goes in the fridge and add a little more honey if it needs it.
health_notes: The protein here is real, but so is the fat: paneer and dark chocolate are both fat-dense, and a serving lands near 540 calories. That is dessert, not a protein snack. Split it three ways rather than two and it becomes a sensible after-dinner portion at around 360 calories.

source.title: High Protein Chocolate Mousse | Try It Or Trash It
source.adapted: Ingredients and method are as shown in the video. The nutrition figures are not: the video claims 780 calories and 65 g protein for the batch, and 65 g is not reachable from 200 g of paneer or tofu. Recalculated from the ingredient list at roughly 1075 calories and 52 g protein for the batch with full-fat paneer, or 775 calories and 44 g with firm tofu - the video's calorie figure matches the tofu version. Chilling time is given as the video's stated 2 hour minimum; the video itself waited three hours.
